Full Metal Schoolgirl is a really fun and funny action game, but unfortunately it's held back by two major things. One is that the camera gets extremely awful whenever you have to do any platforming, which makes the platforming much harder. The other is that it takes inspiration from roguelikes and so most of your powerups on each run are randomized, but unfortunately the majority of main weapons (guns) are complete crap, so you often end up still using a gun from twenty floors ago...

Anyway, if you can get past those issues I recommend it, though not for the asking price of $50. It's a good game, just it's a good "wait for a sale" game.

Alright, so, they fixed the issue where being near traps caused your camera sensitivity to skyrocket, so the game's not practically unplayable in sections anymore.

Anyway, the game's actually pretty fun. It's made by YUKE'S, which are the devs responsible for Earth Defense Force Iron Rain and World Brothers. Fortunately, the shooting feels much more like the latter.

As a rogue-lite, it has some problems. The runs are too long (like, 1.5-2 hours per stint), and mods (the passive items) are far too infrequently dropped/found and often practically useless (seriously, I had one run where I found just [i]one[/i] mod), so it's hard to make any particular build. Also, most mods are pretty boring stat increases (and all of them also come with a minor decrease, making a lot of them seem more detrimental than useful, if the buff is on something you don't care about). I don't think there's any boss variation either, but each stint is pretty much a set of 20-ish floors with a boss at the end. After each first boss kill, you return to base to upgrade and then go back to do another set of floors.

The game's kind of strange in that rather than a pure rogue-lite, it's more of game with segmented progression with randomized floor layouts and drops. You don't start from zero each run (unless you want to), and as mentioned, the game forces you home after each first boss kill.

You're given consumable items to use elevators use from the lobby to skip to higher floors (most of them boss floors - in which case you skip the boss on that particular floor and get immediate access to the boss chests, which mostly appropriately equip you for the coming floors) and continue from there rather than having to start from the ground floor and work your way up all the floors again. That said, you [i]could[/i] start from ground, but it would take way too much time for pretty much no benefit.

That said, weapons are fun. Melee weapons pretty much are just an axe, a sword, or a chainsaw with some slight variations on properties depending on variants you pick up, but every weapon in a melee class pretty much plays the same. Drones have a few varieties, but mostly it's picking between a buff, a stationary turret, a following turret, or drone that shoots at what you're aiming at. I 

Guns are really where the game gets more variation. There's four categories: Machine guns, shotguns, grenade launchers, and snipers. [i]Most[/i] of the weapons in each category will play pretty similarly, but not all. There's some weird stuff out there, such as a "sniper" that's a big box that launches relatively slow, but high damage, business cards and can be charged to shotgun out up to 6 shots at a time. That said, I pretty much always found myself using a pretty vanilla sniper (most of them have piercing) or occasionally a machine gun. Though, on the final boss I used a sniper that has sticky shock rounds.

There's also shields, which you can use to block bullets, but in general, they're mostly stat-sticks (they greatly impact your total HP). Shields can have different coverages, from just frontal, all the way to 360 degree. Wider is generally better, because not only does it allow you to block from more angles, but also because the control is kind of bad. Your character will raise her shield in front of her rather than in the direction you're aiming, so if you're sprinting to the left, she'll raise the shield to the left (and you camera will snap to the direction she's facing), which is pretty annoying, but not a huge deal due to how infrequent you'll probably use the shield. With a 360 degree shield, aside from the camera whipping around, this becomes a non-issue for correctly blocking things.

Anyway, as said, the game's fun. so it's not too hard to recommend as a kind of mindless chaotic rogue-lite shooter.

That said, if it bothers you, there's a whole black void censor under the girls' skirts, but honestly, you generally won't notice it during normal play, because it only fades-in if you low-angle the camera, so it's not distracting as something that stands out as out of place unless you're intentionally looking. You might see it when shooting at fliers, but you're probably going too focused on center-screen to notice unless you're looking for it.

Also, the English translation is pretty bad, as far as translating what the characters are saying is concerned. That said, it does have English voices as an option, so that could be forgiven as a lip sync limitation in some cases, but not all of them (such as during gameplay, where the character's mouth doesn't actually move, or with characters over the phone). It's pretty far off in a fair number of cases, where it's pretty much just, "these two statements in different languages are vaguely alike in tone," rather than a proper translation at all.

Game gets worse as you go on. Started off pretty good... this is basically a Simple Series title off of the PS2. Very basic, very repetitive. But the gameplay itself is pretty mindless fun. However, the fun factor falls off a cliff around floor 50. The amount of AoEs and traps you have to dodge in EVERY room is nonsensical. The mini bosses throw AoEs. There are traps all over the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ floor. There is an abundance of objects blocking your shots. Past that, the amount of traps that spawn out of thin air is insane. You try to do a 180 with the mouse trying to run away from it, and you end up doing a 360 because the mouse sensitivity randomly doubles in certain scenarios, like around these traps that appear out of thin air and in areas with bottomless pits.

Somehow the bosses themselves are a complete joke. They're the easiest part of the game by far. 

Punishment moves punish YOU more than the enemy. Get used to taking damage the MILLISECOND you come out of the animation. The rocket one in particular... yeah just shoot all those rockets at the same enemy 5000 times instead of killing everything. Great idea... Why would I use anything but the default ones? 

MODs are really boring. Gain slightly more of something and lose a bit of something else. Almost makes me not want to use any of them other than the MJP increase ones. 

Platforming is HORRENDOUS and is required for a majority of the game.

 What is the point of offering two different challenges in rooms when you will choose the second one every single time? You have a choice between: 1. Do a challenge for 1x money. 2. Do the same challenge with a very slightly harder requirement for 2x money. Often times this extra requirement is something you won't even think about while clearing the room, like "Don't run out of energy"... I was gonna do that anyway since the best way to avoid damage in this game is to stay as far away from enemies as you possibly can, shooting everything and only using melee when necessary. 

The weapons also feel incredibly ineffective. Accuracy is non-existent unless you're directly in the enemies' face or using a sniper. Use a gatling gun or shotgun? The next room will have two laser turrets that do half of your health and you have to run up to them to do any form of damage. Use a sniper? Well you have to kill 30 enemies one-by-one and you'll end up taking damage from traps trying to dodge everything. 

The enemies are annoying and tanky. The bomber ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, they might be the worst. WHY in god's name do their dynamites having heat-seeking capabilities once they die? It's like everything in this game is designed to deal nonsense damage to you. 

It's a shame, because the style of the game is excellent, along with the soundtrack. Not recommended for the price.

Really surprisingly fun action roguelite shooter. I love the EDF games, the World Brother games, and the Oneechanbara series, so this was on my radar on that alone, but I'm surprised to say that it is a shockingly more polished and cohesive game than a lot of those.

It's a third-person shooter that's tonally really similar to Hi-Fi Rush, as you ascend a tower while fighting the various department heads of an evil corporation. The jokes are predictable but a few have gotten a laugh out of me. What's more surprising to me is that the shooting and general presentation is quite good. Enemies fall apart as you take off limbs, but will continue to try to fight. Rooms get completely torn apart with props flying everywhere. Overall the animation and graphical quality is really nice for this kind of game, way beyond what I've come to expect from D3. (Which sounds like a backhanded compliment. It is, but I mean it.)

That said, the roguelite structure is fun, but definitely seems like it might grate eventually. Most upgrades you find are miniscule bonuses to one stat or another. This is definitely not Gunfire Reborn or Deadzone Rogue. There's still some fun, weird guns to be found that will profoundly change a playthough. My favorites have been a grenade launcher that launches persistent, burning orbs and a gatling gun that fires bullets that bounce off walls. It's fun, but doesn't seem like it will last for dozens of hours.

If anything about this game seems interesting, I think it's an easy recommendation... at like $20-30. 50 is complete nuts lol. Do not pay that. But it will be on sale, and when it is, I think this is really worth checking out.

(Oh, and anyone seriously complaining about "censorship" in a game that is identical across all platforms and regions shouid really, really schedule some time this weekend to call their mom and have a good catch-up. You'll feel better, I promise.)

This is really fun, this reminds me of so many different old games on the PS2, the PS3 and the PS Vita. It's just simple fun with cute characters, a nice core gameplay loop and a really big dungeon. I was worried it'd start to grate on my but by floor 50 I was still being surprised by the gimmicks and traps. It's a bit janky but if you're like an oldschool gamer you'll immediately gel with the control scheme and blow right through it. I'm not the best so I find the normal mode difficulty fairly challenging, but I imagine for pros they'd want to stick the difficulty higher if possible. The nice thing about a game like this is you can easily do self-imposed challenge runs, like not upgrading your character's HP/defense and avoiding items that buff it, you could probably turn the game into a no-hit run type game. 

I saw there's some drama that you can't look up the characters's skirts because the game hides their under-parts?  but I'm not really here to look at that, I'm here because I think robot girls are cool and roguelite dungeon crawlers are cool, I'm sure someone will mod it anyway.

Highly recommend this if you love dungeon crawlers and oldschool hack and slash and robot girls

EDIT: I'm nearly at the top now and there's some great characters and dialogue in this too, the acting is really fun on the JP side. I love the gatling gun with bouncing bullets it rules for clearing corners. Also pro tip anyone who plays this, once you get the double jump, if you spot any scaffolding you can hop on top of it and get inside a vent to cut through a bunch of a floor. This is huge for runbacks, this game really rewards understanding its quirks. Love it.

A roguelike with a very unique style, ultimately brought down by a very steep price tag (50€, 45€ with the launch discount) and no run variety. I got it for cheaper on a website at 28€ and I'm fairly happy with that price, I'd feel scammed if I paid full price of 45€ for it.

The ONLY upgrades you get during a run are just modifiers to your stats, no new abilities, no gameplay-changing buffs, nothing. Just up and down stats. HP, Energy, PP, Critical Rate, Critical Damage, Shooting DMG, Melee DMG, etc, nothing interesting. Theres 3 melee weapon types, despite there being space for a 4th, and 4 gun types (in which the grenade launcher sucks in all regards). There are variety within each type, as theres many different versions of each, but ultimately they do not change how you play. There is also zero feedback from your side when you shoot them, despite the guns being very powerful and the main way to dispatch of the hordes of workbots, you feel like you are shooting a peashooter because your character does not have any kind of shooting animation where the gun shakes, even for visual, she just stands and shoots without any animation cue, regardless of weapon type. Her running and walking animation while holding the gun arm out also feels really stiff compared to when she isn't holding it.

The enemies at least, do react very well to your shots (except for the turrets), their bodies wobble and shake from the part you shoot at them, often losing limbs and having to crawl on the floor to try to stop you or else they'll lose their 24 hour job! There is also good enough variety so far and new enemy types have been introduced after each floor change (boss encounter). This brings me to lack of telling where ranged enemies are, mainly the turrets and fliers. Sure theres a minimap, but if I am looking at the minimap I don't see what I have in front of me, there needs to be better tells for turret enemies before they sniper you from afar. The turrets are extremely annoying they really should've added laser pointers at the player, at least for the most dangerous ones, mainly the rocket turrets and the laser beam turrets, the rockets home in and the lasers slow you down heavily, while being able to hit from very far... Very poorly designed. Just like the Kamikazes from Serious Sam, or something similar, bots with dynamite for hands that suicide on top of you or when you kill them the dynamite bounces around the room, usually homing towards your location in a very strange manner... I've not had any problem with enemies, but these can be extremely annoying considering how small some rooms are.

Dodging sucks. Period. The only way to get a perfect dodge is to stand still and press dodge, you can't get a perfect dodge by dodging into any direction, only neutral. Why? Who thought this be ok?

The main loop and idea of an ever-changing tower and you having to upgrade yourself before runs is pretty solid. Its quite fun, but for the asking price? Theres not enough variety for a roguelike and I don't think this is gonna change the further I get, YUKE'S always seems to half-deliver with their games despite having a very solid base, its like they forget to add elements to it to make it truly shine.

The game's poor mods and lack of any kind of interesting gameplay-changing bonuses really hurt it as you are approaching the last set of floors. The mods are soooo boring. The guns have such uninteresting modifiers. Even when legendary there's nothing legendary about them except the fact that weapons have one more basic stat upgrade.

Wait for a 50% off sale or get it cheaper online. I'd say at 30-ish € would've been a way fairer price to ask for the game.

Lots of upgrades and the shooting feels good, the melee is fun even though it uses energy. You can upgrade it. Game runs perfectly and is overall a simple fun roguelike that is being slightly review bombed due to gooners not being able to look up a girls skirt.

 Build variety is almost nonexistent, despite having 4 categories of item to decide between, the differences are negligible, and usually just consist of raw stats. The one category that might actually make a difference is inundated with many near-worthless things, and there are no banishes, so aiming for specific things is a relatively fruitless endeavor. Most of the time, you're going to want sniper-like weapons. The elevator system is also poorly done; bosses and tough enemies can sometimes drop single use keys that allow you to start on higher floors, however, you start with almost nothing in exchange, putting you at an increasing deficit the higher you go. As a roguelite, its honestly kind of a failure. My biggest complaint, though, is the WILDLY fluctuating mouse sensitivity, added onto the way some traps seems to take control of your camera away, often forcing you to get hit.

Also, just side note, the main bad guy needed to be a bit more active, prerecorded messages or something. He was great in his limited screentime, but he had little presence otherwise.

However, despite those flaws, its still fun. It certainly shares a fair bit of DNA with Earth Defense Force, you'll be against plenty of enemies at a time, and have several super moves at your disposal for clearing the hordes. The platforming and hazards are annoying at first, but you soon unlock skills to make dealing with them much easier. The story is okay, the world it suggests is much more interesting than the actual plot is. It could make for an interesting new franchise, should they take the time to make improvements to the gameplay. The characters are all fun, and that ending was one of the most *anime* ones I've ever encountered in a game.

Edit: I've tried out the harder difficulties, and they seem to, rather than buff health or damage, instead make the enemies attack [i]faster[/i]. Thats great, and much preferable to the way games often deal with difficulty

Edit: Professor Hakase is a man, and it's important for one of the plot lines. They hid their ♥♥♥♥♥♥ politics until the very last character who has lore. This has lost a very large amount of my respect, and as such, I'm changing my review from positive to negative. I had intended to purchase DLC to support the developers I thought highly of, but that will no longer happen, either.

How about instead of complaining that you can't look up underage girls' skirts, or complaining that a Japanese game is sexualizing them like you didn't know that's [i]exactly[/i] what you were signing up for when you bought this thing, we review the actual game please?

Full Metal Schoolgirl is a roguelite shooter where you fight through a 100-floor dungeon. The gameplay's fun, the writing can be pretty entertaining, and the voice acting isn't perfect, but is actually pretty good, which was a pleasant surprise. If you like what the game looks like on the tin, you'll enjoy it... mostly. There's one major gripe and a big performance issue to caveat everything with, but I'm setting this review as a recommend because it [i]is[/i] a fun game, there's just some tedium to get through, and your mileage may vary with the performance issues.

So, why do I not feel this game is an outright recommend? The runs are [i]waaay[/i] too long. Even with the shortcut system, which requires a consumable item to use that demands you complete a completely separate run just to earn, these segments just take forever, and there's no way to suspend if you need to stop halfway through. Either you cashout and "retire" to keep any metaprogression currencies you've acquired, or you keep pushing until you either beat the next story boss or die.

Each section that you'll be doing a run through is about 20 floors, which takes 1-2 hours to complete in my experience so far. So if you're sitting down to make progress, you'd better make sure you're ready to commit to spending the next 2 hours playing this. If you don't wanna spend a keycard, then you'll probably be running through 2 sections, so double that to about 3 hours. It feels ludicrously long, and losing an hour's worth of progress to a major boss absolutely [i]suuuucks[/i] when it's forcing you to replay that much content to make it back. The worst part is, the metaprogression doesn't actually make you stronger, you can get minor upgrades to max HP, or more slots for your typical roguelite artefacts, but nothing you can buy will improve how fast you'll be clearing a room outright. So just know that playing this game, you're signing up for a big commitment each session, and it's never really gonna get quicker.

All that said, the gameplay's great. The characters are charismatic, wacky and fun. The roguelite pressure is balanced hard enough to get you to fail, but is light enough that it'll only take you one or two attempts to break through that barrier, so you're never gonna hit a brick wall in progress. The only other caveat to mention is that there's something wrong with the performance on larger floors. I don't know if the game's not culling physics objects properly or what's going on, but there's definitely an issue on any floor with a lot of objects loaded, so maybe drop the draw distance and see if that helps if you run into it. It tends to kick in for me on floors 20-30 so far.

I was a bit apprehsive on this game. On the one hand, robots with bigass weapons tearing apart other robots? Sign me the hell up! On the other hand... schoolgirls... eugh.

After playing this game for some time though, I can say that's been pretty fun. It's not the most well-polished or thought out, but it has a unique concept and executes on that well enough.

There are two problems with the game though. One is that it's not so subtly suggestive at times. And considering the protags... well, do I need to spell it out for you? It's not that big of a deal, but it is something I found myself turning a blind eye at every time it showed up.

The second problem is the heavy punishment of death. This a rougelite that requires to go through a 100-floor building. While the time between floors isn't long (especially if you're gunning for the exit), 100 floors is still 100 floors. There are checkpoints but they're one-time use, so if you ♥♥♥♥ up and kill a run your ass is getting sent back to the beginning. F u n.

The game is good enough on its own, but the two issues stated above make this a hesitant recommend. Which is a shame, because the gameplay is hella fun. If you're willing to overlook them, get the game. If not, well, give it a shot, but I will not blame you for passing this one.

Rougelite shooter with hack-and-slash elements. The price point is probably a tough buy for anyone, and I would recommend waiting for a sale, though at that point I would recommend any EDF game over this. [strike]It's good, but a specific kind of good that I don't know how to recommend.[/strike]

That's probably why the game was marketed as "[i]a game that combines the close combat of "Onechanbara” with the gun battles of 'Earth Defense Force'[/i]” and I kinda agree with that sentiment due to how chaotic encounters can get and the enemy variety. 

I am currently in a hack-and-slash + character action craze so there was some expectation to fill that on my part. The available hack-an-slash elements are obviously not as deep as OneeChanbara, but I was at least hoping for the '[i]cool combo[/i]' system to be in this game because of that marketing statement. Melee is a bit weird overall, acting as crowd control and or supplementary damage based on which you choose/ are given. You do have the perfect dodging (but much riskier) and ults that exist similarly in OneeChanbara so I guess there's that. 

[h3]PROS: [/h3][list]
[*]Good visuals
[*]Humour
[*]Despite there only being 4 gun types, there is good variety in rarer variants
[*]Challenging level of difficulty (though I am also adjusting to aim with a controller for this game)
[*]Satisfying [strike]combat[/strike] weapons
[/list]

[h3]CONS: [/h3][list]
[*]overall repetitiveness
[*]camera panning after every encounter
[*]repetitive stage music
[*][strike]so many button bindings (driving me away from keyboard/ mouse)[/strike]
[*]MODs give downsides
[*]Item drop variety is kinda terrible... I'm never getting enough MODs in my runs to filling out my inventory unless I start at a previous checkpoint (and spent like 40 minutes to get back).
[*]Very long run time but at least itautosaves
[*]Ults leave you very vulnerable and are hard to use in the floors because the i-frames end as soon as they do
[*]Unbalanced economy, you get way too much money but not enough materials to use it. This applies before finishing the game.
[*][strike]Upgrades feel skewed to improving survivability over making me feel more powerful.[/strike]
[/list]

Got this game when it came out. Played it for about 2 hours so far and so far I've enjoyed it. It's a fun hack n slash/shooter game. I've so far managed to make it up to the 10th floor. I enjoy some of the lines from the enemy bots. Though I can see that it may feel a bit repetitive the longer I play, but til I feel that, I enjoy this game and recommend if you like roguelite games, going in, going so far, dieing, upgrading yourself, going back in to try to get further and more resources for more upgrades.
